To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
IRGM is associated with CD in Europeans, but not in Japanese.

the CD risk variants in the IRGM region are in strong LD with a 20 kb CNV upstream of IRGM, and that this deletion is in strong LD with two independent variants in IRGM itself, a promoter insertion/deletion polymorphism, and an insertion/deletion polymor-phism in the 5′ untranslated exon, and that the risk haplotype, but not the CNV or the 5′ UTR variants, is associated with decreased expression of IRGM, but only
the IRGM locus is associated with CD and that the CD risk variants are in strong LD with the IRGM deletion, which was recently reported to be in LD with the CD-associated IRGM variants.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the genetic architecture of a region on chromosome band 5q33 that contains two genes, IRGM and ZNF300, which are associated with Crohns disease, a common inflammatory disorder of the gastrointestinal tract.
the genetic basis of Crohn's disease, a common form of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) which is characterized by chronic inflammation of the intestinal tract.

the identification of the genetic factors that contribute to the pathogenesis of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) and the understanding of the mechanisms underlying the genetic association of these factors with the disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is an independent association of the IRGM locus and CD, but the precise causal variant remains to be determined.
the IRGM locus is associated with CD, but that the mechanism of association is complex and likely to be population-specific.
the IRGM locus has a population-specific association with CD.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

1) IRGM is a CD susceptibility gene; 2) IRGM expression is decreased in CD patients; 3) the IRGM risk variant is in LD with a CNV; 4) the IRGM deletion is not the true causal variant; 5) the IRGM insertion–deletion polymorphisms are associated with CD; 6) the IRGM CNV and 5′-UTR variant −308(GT)5 are independent risk factors; and
we have identified a number of variants at the IRGN locus that are associated with CD, but that the association is not universal and may be population specific.

the IRGM locus is a major risk locus for CD; the risk is mediated by multiple independent variants in this region; the risk haplotype decreases IRGM expression; and that the association of the risk haplote with CD is population-specific.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the IRGM risk variant is population-specific.
, while it is possible to find strong association of a gene with a disease, this association does not necessarily imply that the gene is causal.
the IRGM locus is a complex region with multiple variants that are associated with CD, but the variants are population-specific.
